story.title: A small room for a quiet craft
paragraphs: Kumo means cloud: something that changes every day and never looks the same twice. So does our counter. What we serve depends on what the fish market had that morning.
We season the rice with red vinegar, keep it at body temperature and shape each piece by hand. You eat it the moment it is set down, the way it is meant to be.

omakase.title: “I leave it to you”
omakase.intro: Omakase is a conversation with the chef. Here is how the evening goes.

steps.title: Book your seats
steps.text: Call or message us on Zalo at least a day ahead, and tell us about allergies or what you don't eat.

steps.title: Sit at the counter
steps.text: The chef works in front of you. Ask anything: the fish, where it comes from, why this piece now.

steps.title: One piece at a time
steps.text: Each nigiri is already seasoned: no extra soy sauce needed. Eat it by hand or with chopsticks, in one bite.

steps.title: Close with something warm
steps.text: Soup, a hand roll, then dessert and tea. About two hours, never rushed.

omakase.note: Omakase seatings: 18:00 and 20:15. Please arrive on time: the first pieces are served together.

items.a: For omakase, yes: at least one day ahead, by phone or Zalo. À la carte at lunch, walk-ins are welcome when seats are free.
Tell us when you book (shellfish, gluten, raw fish…). The chef adapts the course where the dish allows it.
We can prepare a vegetable omakase with a day's notice. The à la carte rolls also have vegetable versions.
For the Chef's counter course and groups of six or more, we ask for a deposit when you book; we explain how when you call.
Children are welcome at lunch. The omakase counter suits guests from 12 years old.
